questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder.
Check your mirrors. You only need to look over your shoulder if something seems wrong.
Either check your mirrors or look over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and look over your shoulder. Make sure no other vehicles are in your path.

questions.question: How should you brake?
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: A motorcycle's horn is ________ a car's horn.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's horn is not as loud as other vehicle horns. Use your horn when needed, but do not rely on it for safety.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers that right turns are not allowed in this area. It is a white sign with red and black markings that shows traffic rules.

questions.question: Alcohol reaches the brain ________ being consumed.
questions.explanation: Alcohol affects your brain and riding ability within minutes of drinking. Riding a motorcycle while impaired by alcohol is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: When riding ________, you face the greatest danger from other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Intersections are where most motorcycle and vehicle conflicts happen. Position yourself in a lane where other drivers can see you clearly.

questions.question: If you have been drinking and wait one hour per drink before riding:

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your riding skills will not be affected.
You may still have side effects from drinking.
You will be fine as long as you ride slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may still have side effects from drinking.
questions.explanation: Your body eliminates about one drink's worth of alcohol per hour. But even with waiting, alcohol can still affect your judgment and abilities.

questions.question: You should leave more space between you and the vehicle ahead:

options.text: If you can see through the vehicles ahead to check traffic.

questions.explanation: Leave extra space if the pavement is slippery, if you cannot see ahead, or if traffic is heavy. Use at least a four-second following distance in these situations.

questions.question: The best formation when riding in a group:
questions.explanation: Staggered formation is usually best for group riding. Switch to single-file when turning, entering a highway, leaving a highway, or taking curves.

questions.question: Stopping while turning is difficult because:

options.text: The leaning motorcycle has less grip available for stopping.
The rider is focused on turning, not on braking.
The brakes do not work when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: The leaning motorcycle has less grip available for stopping.
questions.explanation: You can brake while turning, but it takes skill. When the motorcycle is leaning for the turn, some grip is already being used. This leaves less grip for braking.

questions.question: Your lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Make it easier for others to see you.
Encourage other drivers to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Encourage other drivers to share your lane.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps others see you and helps you see them. It also helps you avoid wind from other vehicles, blind spots, and road hazards. Your lane position should discourage other drivers from entering your lane and give you a way to escape if danger appears.

questions.question: To reduce the chances of a collision, you should:

options.text: Focus only on your riding, not on what is around you.

questions.explanation: Wearing bright or reflective clothing makes you easier to see and reduces crash risk. Always watch the drivers around you so you can predict what they will do next.

questions.question: A motorcyclist is usually most easily seen by other drivers when riding in which lane position?
questions.explanation: The center lane position is usually best when following a car. It places you in the driver's rearview mirror where they can see you. Be ready to change positions if traffic or road conditions require it.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The traffic light is about to turn red.
The traffic light is about to turn green.
Stop and wait for traffic to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The traffic light is about to turn red.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow light warns that the signal will change to red soon. Slow down and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection when it turns yellow, continue through.

questions.question: If you will be carrying a passenger on your motorcycle, you will likely have to:

options.text: Make no changes to tire pressure.

questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle. You will need to add a few pounds of pressure to your tires before riding. Check your owner's manual for the correct pressure to use.

questions.question: When wearing a jacket for protection, the jacket should:

options.text: Be loose and flap in the wind while riding.

questions.explanation: Riding clothes should protect you and keep you comfortable. Jackets and pants should fit snug enough that they do not flap in the wind, but loose enough that you can move freely.

questions.question: When riding at night, maintain a minimum following distance of:
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge distances at night. Keep at least three seconds of following distance when riding after dark.

questions.question: The single most important thing you can do to improve your chances of surviving a crash is to:

options.text: Wear a high-quality helmet that is securely fastened.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear a high-quality helmet that is securely fastened.
questions.explanation: Wearing a high-quality helmet that is securely fastened is the single best thing you can do to survive a crash.

questions.question: Before starting a turn, a motorcyclist should change gears to:

options.text: Prevent a sudden change in engine power during the turn.
Keep both hands on the handle grips during the turn.
Keep the motorcycle from slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent a sudden change in engine power during the turn.
questions.explanation: Change gears before you start a turn. Shifting while turning can cause sudden engine power changes that make the rear wheel skid. If you must shift during a turn, shift smoothly to avoid skidding.

questions.question: If you borrow a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Assume all controls are in the same places as on your motorcycle.
Take it right out on the highway.
Practice with it in a safe, controlled area.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice with it in a safe, controlled area.
questions.explanation: Every motorcycle is different. Before riding a new motorcycle, learn where all the controls are. Practice in a safe area until you feel comfortable before taking it on the road.

questions.question: What is a good way to handle a tailgater?
questions.explanation: The best way to deal with a tailgater is to let them pass you. Speeding up will only make them tailgate you at a higher speed, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: Should you wear gloves while riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Yes. Your hands may get cold while riding.
Yes. They improve grip and protect your hands.
No. Gloves can interfere with the controls.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes. They improve grip and protect your hands.
questions.explanation: Wearing gloves improves grip and protects your hands. Use full-fingered gloves made of durable material.

questions.question: What color are service signs?
questions.explanation: Blue signs with white letters show where services are located. Services include rest areas, gas stations, food, and hospitals.

questions.question: When someone is passing you on the left, what should you do?

options.text: Ride on the right side of your lane.
Ride in the center of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed on your left, ride in the center of your lane. Riding on the right side can encourage the passing driver to return to your lane too quickly, which is dangerous.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a potential problem?

options.text: Conditions that do not change as you get closer

questions.correctAnswerText: Conditions that do not change as you get closer
questions.explanation: Look for potential problems on the roadway and make a plan to reduce their risks. Conditions that stay the same are not a problem.

questions.question: What is unique about how alcohol enters the bloodstream?

options.text: It enters the bloodstream very quickly.
It must be digested before entering the bloodstream.

questions.correctAnswerText: It enters the bloodstream very quickly.
questions.explanation: Alcohol enters the bloodstream directly through the stomach and small intestine. It does not need to be digested first. It reaches the brain quickly.

questions.question: Before riding, check your clutch. A good clutch should feel:
questions.explanation: Before riding, check your clutch and throttle. The throttle should snap back when released. The clutch should feel tight and smooth.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions. This sign warns of a divided roadway ahead.

questions.question: What kind of footwear should a motorcycle rider wear?
questions.explanation: Wear sturdy boots that cover and support your ankles. The soles should be hard, durable, and slip-resistant.

questions.question: What should you do before riding an unfamiliar motorcycle for the first time?

options.text: Just start riding. Learning by doing is best.
Just start riding. Most bikes are similar.
Practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes to learn how the bike works.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes to learn how the bike works.
questions.explanation: Every motorcycle is different. Before riding an unfamiliar bike, check its safety and maintenance. Learn where everything is. Practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes to understand how it works.
